content.intro: This lesson focuses on null and missing values and connects the PDF syllabus topics to a small, inspectable example. Work from the intended data model, write down the expected result, then verify syntax and semantics with the target tool.
content.why_it_matters: Null and Missing Values matters because structured-data files sit between people, tools, services, and deployment systems. A clear contract and repeatable checks make the result easier to maintain and safer to consume.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: JSON strings use double quotes and defined escapes; numbers follow a strict grammar; booleans are lowercase literals; and null differs from a missing member. Parsers create runtime values that can have language-specific numeric and null behavior.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Null and Missing Values
content_blocks.expected_output: The fields represent different states: explicit null, an empty string, and an empty array. A missing object member is a fourth distinct state.
